To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the recent five-factor model and four-factor model fail to explain returns to characteristic and covariance pure plays.
the recent Fama- French five-factor model and the Hou-Xue-Zang four-factor model fail in explaining the time series of characteristic and covariance pure plays, which is a new test for factor models.

(1) Fama-French and Hou-Xue Zhang factor models fail on characteristic and covariance pure plays, (2) the failure is especially pronounced for momentum-neutral portfolios and investment, and (3) the failure is economically significant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the empirical performance of factor models in explaining the cross-section of returns.
the empirical relevance of the recent Fama French five factor model and the Hou, Xue, and Zhang four factor model.
the empirical validity of factor models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the factor models are not good at explaining returns to investment, momentum-neutral portfolios, and pure plays.
the models are not good at explaining the cross-section of stock returns.
the Fama-French and Hou-Xue Zhang models do not explain returns well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the factor models do not explain the cross-section of stock returns as well as the CAPM.
factor models are useful in explaining average cross-sectional returns but are not as successful in explaining returns to characteristics and covariances.
the Fama-French and Hou-XueZhang models are good in explaining average cross-sectional returns, but not so good in explaining cross-sectional variation in expected returns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the factor models do not explain the time series of asset returns as well as they claim to.
the Fama-French and Hou-Xue Zhang factor models do not fully explain returns.
the factor models do not fully explain the time series and cross-sectional variation of returns.
